io.reader

Class ReadCSV

  • java.lang.Object
    • io.reader.ReadCSV
  • All Implemented Interfaces:
    Readable, java.lang.AutoCloseable, java.lang.Iterable<java.lang.String[]>

    public class ReadCSV
extends java.lang.Object
implements Readable
    Reads CSV files into memory using a quote-aware state-machine parser that supports quoted fields, escaped quotes, and multiline records.

    Implements Readable and Iterable for uniform table processing. The base class automatically sanitises internal newlines during row processing. Subclasses can override processHeader(String[]) or extend processRow(String[], int) to apply custom validation, schema checking, or domain-specific data transformations.

    Change log:
    • 7 February 2025 - Initial creation as AbstractCSVReader.
    • 8 October 2026 - Re-factored to concrete ReadCSV in io.reader, added RFC 4180 multi-line record parsing, and integrated TabularDataException.
    • 10 October 2026 - Updated matrix column sizing to evaluate maximum row width across the whole document.
    Since:
    7 February 2025

      • processRow

        protected void processRow(java.lang.String[] rowTokens,
                          int lineNumber)
        Executes post-processing on each parsed content row greater than zero (first row) position.

        The base implementation flattens embedded line breaks into single spaces and trims cell values. Subclasses overriding this method should invoke super.processRow(rowTokens, lineNumber) if they wish to retain default string sanitisation prior to executing custom validation.

        Parameters:
        rowTokens - array of raw cell tokens for the current record
        lineNumber - 1-based data row index (where header is row 0)

      • parseDataCSV

        private java.lang.String[] parseDataCSV(java.io.BufferedReader br)
                                 throws java.io.IOException
        Parses a single multi-line CSV record from a BufferedReader according to RFC 4180. Handles quotes, escaped quotes (""), embedded newlines, custom whitespace (including NBSP), and leading/trailing unquoted trimming.
        Parameters:
        br - BufferedReader stream positioned at the record start
        Returns:
        String[] representing tokenised field values, or null if EOF reached
        Throws:
        java.io.IOException - if an unterminated double-quoted field is encountered
